Is the total 75 or more? Give the total in the evidence.
   "tn14": Over the last five years, has revenue grown every year, operating margin expanded, free cash flow been positive and rising, and cash exceeded debt every year?

summaries.gardner: Southern Company is a century-old regulated utility, the opposite of a Rule Breaker: it leads a mature industry, its advantage is a government-granted monopoly rather than innovation, and its name is not a consumer brand. The AI data-center power boom adds a growth story, but it misses most of Gardner's traits.
summaries.buffett: Southern fits Buffett's taste for simple, durable, regulated monopolies like Berkshire Hathaway Energy, with exclusive territories in Georgia, Alabama and Mississippi and 25 straight years of dividend increases. But it earns modest returns on a huge capital base, has negative free cash flow (2025: $9,802M operating cash flow vs $12,737M property additions), carries about $75.6B of debt, and at about 22x trailing earnings offers no margin of safety.
summaries.munger: Munger would see a sturdy, essential franchise with few ways to fail outright, but also a business whose returns are capped by regulators and which constantly needs new capital. It is a fair business at a full price rather than a wonderful business at a fair price.
summaries.lynch: Lynch would class Southern as a slow grower or stalwart bought mainly for its dividend (3.04 per share annualized, about 3.3% yield). With a P/E around 22 and adjusted EPS growth of about 6% in 2025 ($4.30 vs $4.05), it fails his P/E-to-growth test, and it is widely owned rather than overlooked.
summaries.fisher: Fisher prized companies with long sales runways and strong R&D; Southern has a demand runway from data centers and Southeast growth, but sells a commodity at regulated prices and has little product development. Its management depth and long-range planning fit some of his points, but not the innovation ones.
summaries.graham: Southern passes Graham's tests for size, an unbroken dividend record (paid every quarter for 79 consecutive years) and ten years of profits, with EPS up about 51% from 2015 ($2.60) to 2025 ($3.92). It fails on price: about 24x three-year average earnings and P/E times P/B well above 22.5, and its current ratio is below 1.
summaries.thiel: Southern holds a legal monopoly in its territories, which Thiel would value, but it has no proprietary technology and its monopoly profits are capped by regulators. It does not answer Thiel's questions about technology, timing or a secret others miss.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner looks for durable growth at a reasonable price; Southern is a beneficiary of AI-driven power demand but grows earnings only mid-to-high single digits, burns free cash flow on its build-out, and trades at about 20x forward earnings. It is a picks-and-shovels angle on AI, but not a high-growth compounder.
summaries.druckenmiller: Druckenmiller would note improving earnings (first-half 2026 adjusted EPS $2.46 vs $2.15) and a data-center catalyst, but also a stock that fell about 3% over the past year, heavy interest-rate sensitivity and regulatory risk. It is unlikely to be a high-conviction, concentrated bet.
summaries.smith: Fundsmith avoids utilities because they earn low returns on capital, need heavy reinvestment and are price-regulated; Southern's ROIC of about 4-5% and negative free cash flow clearly fail Smith's 'good company' test.
summaries.greenblatt: On the Magic Formula Southern scores poorly: 2025 operating income of $7,285M is only about 4% of an enterprise value near $179B, and returns on its huge tangible capital base are low.
summaries.akre: Akre's three-legged stool needs a high-return business, excellent management and good reinvestment; Southern can reinvest heavily (an $81B five-year capital plan) but only at regulated returns, so the first leg is weak.
summaries.pabrai: Pabrai seeks simple businesses in temporary distress with low downside and high upside; Southern is simple and low-risk, but it is not distressed or cheap, so the upside is limited.
summaries.wood: Southern is not a disruptive innovator; it is a utility that supplies power to AI data centers. It does not fit ARK's focus on companies leading AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or genomics platforms, though rising power demand from AI is relevant to its growth.
summaries.ackman: Ackman likes simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generating businesses with high barriers to entry; Southern has the barriers and predictability, but its negative free cash flow, high leverage and regulator-set returns make it a weaker fit.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep's 'scale economics shared' requires passing scale savings to customers; Southern's prices are set by regulators and have been rising (e.g. Vogtle costs), so it does not fit his model, though its long-term franchise is durable.
summaries.valentine: Valentine looked for huge markets and products solving painful problems at the right time; electricity for AI data centers is a large, timely need, but Southern is an incumbent utility, not an emerging company exploiting a technology shift.
summaries.nash: Southern fails several of Nash's filters: debt far exceeds cash, revenue growth is below 10% in 2026, free cash flow is negative, and interest coverage is only about 2.3x. It is a large US company with a clear AI-power angle, but it scores about 60 on Nash's 13 categories, below the 75 threshold.

momentum.evidence: The share price was about $92.89 in late October 2026, down about 3% over the past 52 weeks per StockAnalysis, lagging the market.

g4.evidence: CEO Chris Womack is an experienced long-time Southern executive, and the stock is about 74% institutionally owned, but it has no famous backer or partner.

g6.evidence: Some commentators call it expensive for a utility at about 22x trailing earnings, but it is not widely viewed as a bubble stock.

simple.evidence: It generates and delivers electricity and gas in its service territories at prices regulated by state commissions.

b2.evidence: It has paid a dividend every quarter for 79 consecutive years and raised it for 25 consecutive years (April 2026).

integrity.evidence: Management is open about plans and runs a steady dividend policy, but the Vogtle 3 and 4 and Kemper projects ran years late and billions over budget.

b6.evidence: Its spending is mostly regulated capacity for customer demand, though the $81B five-year capital plan is huge and partly reflects the industry-wide data-center rush.

roic.evidence: Return on invested capital is only about 4.5% (StockAnalysis), and the business depends on about $75.6B of debt.

fcf.evidence: In 2025 operating cash flow was $9,802M but property additions were $12,737M, leaving free cash flow of about -$2,935M.

b10.evidence: Retained earnings and new capital have built rate base that lifted net income to $4,341M in 2025, but returns on that capital are modest and diluted shares rose from 1,065M (2020) to 1,109M (2025).

safety.evidence: At about 22x trailing earnings and 2.7x book, with negative free cash flow, the price is not well below a conservative estimate of value.

fairprice.evidence: About 20x forward earnings is a premium to the utility sector, though somewhat justified by data-center-driven growth.

mu5.evidence: As a regulated monopoly supplying essential power to about 9 million customers, there are few ways it could fail outright.

reinvest.evidence: It can reinvest heavily for many years (an $81B five-year capital plan), but only at regulator-allowed returns.

ly2.evidence: It is a clear stalwart/slow grower: a regulated utility with steady dividends and added growth from data-center demand.

ly3.evidence: A P/E of about 22 is well above adjusted EPS growth of about 6% in 2025 ($4.30 vs $4.05).

runway.evidence: Consensus expects revenue to grow to about $34.7B by 2028 from $29.6B in 2025, but growth is limited to its franchise territories.

ly7.evidence: Insiders are not notable buyers, and diluted shares have risen from 1,065M (2020) to 1,109M (2025) as it issues equity to fund growth.

ly8.evidence: Utilities are a 'boring' niche, but Southern is a $100B+ company that is widely covered.

fi3.evidence: R&D spending is small and not separately reported in a way that allows judging its results.

fi4.evidence: It has signed about 10 GW of large-load contracts with data centers, but most customers have no choice of supplier.

longterm.evidence: It plans decades ahead with integrated resource plans and long-lived assets such as Vogtle 3 and 4 nuclear units.
